summary:
Khonsu is an interactive web observatory that makes NASA’s SPHEREx infrared observations easier to explore and compare across time. Developed for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, our prototype helps users investigate potential moving objects and changing sources through an immersive interface inspired by rewinding the night sky.

Users can search sky coordinates, explore example targets, and compare observations from different dates. Our Python backend retrieves public data from NASA/IPAC’s Infrared Science Archive, aligns images on a shared celestial coordinate grid, and checks wavelength compatibility and pixel quality. Observation dates, source information, and scientific limitations provide context for interpreting apparent changes without treating them as confirmed discoveries.

Named after the Egyptian lunar deity whose name means “the traveler,” Khonsu combines image processing, interactive visualization, and human curiosity. It lowers the barrier to exploring astronomical data and invites citizen scientists to investigate what time reveals in the infrared sky.
details:
Khonsu is an interactive web observatory that helps citizen scientists explore how the infrared sky changes over time. Built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, it turns public astronomical observations into a visual investigation workflow: choose a sky position, compare real observation dates, inspect image quality, and preserve evidence about features worth investigating.

Users can enter right ascension, declination and field of view, or begin with one of five challenge targets: Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae and R Draconis. The Python backend queries NASA/IPAC’s Infrared Science Archive and downloads bounded SPHEREx spectral-image cutouts. It reads calibrated FITS data, checks approximate wavelength compatibility at the requested position, registers observations on a common celestial coordinate grid, preserves quality masks, and prepares images with recorded display settings. Previously acquired real examples support exploration when the archive is unavailable.

The observation console provides a curved timeline, real-date rewind dragging, playback, frame stepping, pan, zoom and A/B comparison. Users can inspect observation dates, wavelengths, source links and quality information. Candidate marks record sky coordinates, compared observations and source metadata. Observation notes and candidate records can be saved in a private notebook and exported as versioned evidence files. Guided Mode and a field guide explain the controls and scientific limitations.

Optional context layers add Gaia Data Release 3 catalog positions and proper-motion information, an independently labelled AllWISE reference view through CDS Aladin Lite, and NASA Eyes mission context. These resources help users understand a field while preserving the distinction between catalog information, reference imagery and SPHEREx measurements.

Our creative direction grew from the idea of physically rewinding the night sky. Khonsu translates that cinematic gesture into navigation through actual observation dates. An original celestial guardian, planetary illustration, restrained motion and an observatory-style interface make the experience inviting. Scientific frames remain tied to their real timestamps rather than invented intermediate observations.

The frontend uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, CSS Modules, Canvas, WebGL2 and Web Workers, with GSAP and Motion for interface animation. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Astropy, reproject, SciPy and Pillow. SQLite supports an optional notebook copy, and Docker provides a reproducible runtime. The application works in modern desktop and mobile browsers, with CPU rendering available when GPU acceleration is unavailable.

Scientific integrity shaped the design. We considered spectral differences, detector artifacts, missing coverage, native resolution, network failures, resource limits, accessibility and privacy. Clean View and optional refinement provide clearly labelled visual derivatives; original data remains
